cards.headline: A fan remixer from Brooklyn co-wrote it
cards.snippet: In 2014, Brooklyn multimedia artist MeLo-X released Yoncé-X, an EP of remixes of tracks from Beyoncé's self-titled album, and it caught her ear. She invited him to add music to her 2014 On the Run Tour with Jay Z. In 2015 he started travelling to Los Angeles to work with her on what became Lemonade. There he co-wrote and co-produced "Sorry" with Wynter Gordon. He told Pitchfork he wrote it probably in the summer of 2015, well before Justin Bieber's "Sorry" came out.
cards.context: MeLo-X told Pitchfork the track was probably written the summer before Lemonade.

cards.headline: Dancehall roots behind the electro-R&B beat
cards.snippet: MeLo-X, who is Jamaican, tried to work dancehall influences into the track. He called the starting idea "pretty simple": keys, drum patterns, then vocal and lyric ideas. Hit-Boy later added sounds and layers.
cards.context: Recorded at Beehive Studios in Los Angeles. The drums were played on a Roland TR-808.

cards.headline: The video is part of the Lemonade film on HBO
cards.snippet: The "Sorry" video is one segment of Beyoncé's one-hour film Lemonade, which aired on HBO on April 23, 2016. It was released on its own two months later, with a cameo from Serena Williams.
cards.context: Directed by Kahlil Joseph and Beyoncé. It was the first standalone clip released from the film.
